alex: @tess @brian kicking off a PRD intake for a feature I'm calling 'progressive quantized rollouts' — wanting to capture problem statement, goals, non-goals, and clear acceptance criteria.

alex: Problem statement: customers want the cost benefits of quantized model variants but are nervous about quality regressions and cold-start/latency regressions during rollouts. today we either fully switch models (risky) or run separate endpoints (expensive). need a safe, observable staged rollout model that integrates with Redwood routing and evals.

alex: High-level goals:
- let product teams define staged rollouts from FP16/FP32 -> int8/4bit variants with traffic ramps
- automatic evaluation gates using customer/fleet eval sets + canary sampling
- rollback and fallback to higher-fidelity variants on quality/latency regressions
- expose simple Console controls + API for rollout config

alex: Non-goals:
- building new quant algorithms or doing auto-quantization research (we'll support curated quant profiles only)
- replacing model training/finetuning workflows

alex: Proposed success metrics (must be measurable from Redwood telemetry):
- cost: median per-token cost for quantized stage <= baseline * 0.75 (25% savings)
- quality: eval-suite regression rate <= 1% (customer-defined eval set)
- latency: p95 latency increase <= 10ms vs FP baseline for typical seq lengths
- rollout safety: automatic rollback triggers fired < 0.5% of rollouts in first 7 days

alex: Initial acceptance criteria (engineering + product):
```
- runtime can serve quantized variants side-by-side with unquantized models
- Console/API supports rollout config: stages, traffic %, duration, eval-set id
- telemetry emits per-stage metrics: cost, p50/p95 latency, eval pass/fail
- gate engine can compare eval results and trigger rollback/fallback
- docs and migration guide published
```

alex: Edge cases to consider (please add):
- small-batch/no-batching workloads with quantized variants causing latency regressions
- KV cache layout differences between quantized/unquantized models that might hurt prefix warmups
- mixed-tenant rollouts where a tenant pins to older variant
- model incompatibilities where fallback model isn't byte-identical (prompt/response diffs)

tess: runtime questions: what are our compatibility constraints for KV cache across quant levels? switching cache format mid-conversation could be awful. need clear dislike for cross-variant cache sharing.

tess: engineering proposal (short): add variant-aware cache namespace + stage-aware routing. rollout will mark requests with `variant_id` header so cache keys separate.

brian: from ML side: we need curated eval sets per tenant + a standardized calibration harness. also recommend we require two eval sets: internal regression set + customer-provided golden set (if available). thresholds should be configurable per-tenant.

brian: note: some models degrade gracefully at 8-bit, others don't. we'll publish per-model quant profiles (expected quality delta).

olivia: UI notes: Console needs a simple scaffold — "Create rollout" -> choose model variant -> set stages -> attach eval set -> preview expected cost delta and risk level. show recommended defaults and an "advanced" open for power users.

olivia: copy suggestion for the gate confirmation dialog: "This rollout will route X% traffic to a lower-precision variant, which reduces cost but may slightly impact output quality. Redwood will evaluate and automatically revert if regressions are detected."

alex: acceptance criteria addition: rollout config example + API snippet in docs.

alex: sample rollout config (for docs):
```
POST /rollouts
{
  "model": "redwood/llama-compat-v2",
  "variant": "int8-preset-3",
  "stages": [
    {"traffic_pct": 5, "duration_min": 60},
    {"traffic_pct": 25, "duration_min": 120},
    {"traffic_pct": 100, "duration_min": 0}
  ],
  "eval_set_id": "cust-1234-probes",
  "rollback_conditions": {"eval_fail_rate": 0.01, "p95_latency_increase_ms": 10}
}
```

alex: ops question: what SLOs do we promise during progressive rollouts? do Dedicated customers expect stricter guarantees?

sre-bot: Deploy tracker: created rollout-safety-checklist ticket (#INF-2783). link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2783

tess: acceptance tests we need from infra:
- canary sampling correctness (traffic percentages are accurate +-1%)
- telemetry labeling by stage/variant
- simulated degradation test that triggers rollback automatically

brian: eval pipeline tasks:
- add per-tenant eval hooks and baseline snapshot storage
- implement statistical test (bootstrap A/B) to detect degradation beyond threshold

olivia: design tasks:
- mockups for Console create-rollout and status page (showing stage, metrics, diff preview)
- microcopy for rollback and risk descriptions

alex: outstanding decisions for PRD:
- default rollback thresholds (prod-wide) vs tenant override? (proposal: defaults + tenant override with guardrails for hosted tier)
- whether to allow mixed-precision caching (tess said no)
- retention for eval snapshots (30d?)

alex: next steps: I'll draft the PRD doc with the above sections + acceptance checklist. please comment in this thread by EOD Thu. after that we'll schedule a quick 30m sync to finalize acceptance criteria and ship plan.

olivia: lgtm, will add UI mocks by Wed.

tess: will sketch runtime design + rough ETA (2 sprints) after I sync with infra.

brian: will prepare per-model quant profile doc and sample eval sets by next Tue.

alex: thanks all — added action items to INF-2783.
